Code § 1950.5)","requirement":"Landlords may not demand or receive security (any payment, fee, deposit or charge, including tenant-processing charges and advance rent) above one month's rent, in addition to first month's rent, for residential rentals. Small landlords (a natural person, or an LLC whose members are all natural persons, who owns no more than two residential rental properties with no more than four dwelling units in total) are limited to two months' rent, but this higher cap does not apply when the prospective tenant is a service member. Higher-than-standard security charged to a service member on or after 2025-04-01 requires a written explanation, and the excess must be returned after no more than six months if the tenant is not in arrears. Advance payment of six months' rent or more is allowed for a lease term of six months or longer. The landlord must hold the security for the tenant. Deductions are limited to amounts reasonably necessary for default in rent, damage beyond ordinary wear and tear, cleaning to the move-in level, and restoring or returning personal property. The landlord must offer an initial inspection and give 48 hours' notice. The landlord must take photographs at move-in (for tenancies beginning on or after 2025-07-01) and at move-out. Within 21 calendar days after the tenant vacates, the landlord must send an itemized statement with supporting documents and return the remainder of the security. The remainder is returned electronically if the landlord received payments electronically. No deduction documentation is required if deductions are $125 or less, unless the tenant requests it. Security may not be called 'nonrefundable'.","key_value":"1 month's rent cap (2 months for small landlords; not for service-member tenants); return within 21 calendar days","coverage_conditions":"Rental agreements for residential property used as the tenant's dwelling.
